before:
Tidal Slipway Association — Winter Haul-Out Allocation

The cradle and tractor are available to all members holding a current mooring ticket, and every craft on the register may be lifted at some point during the closed season. When more requests arrive than the November tide windows allow, the yard foreman works down the list in a settled order: working boats are lifted before club dinghies, and club dinghies before visiting craft. No craft is refused on this ground alone; those not lifted in November are carried forward to the December windows and, failing that, to the March slot. Members may still swap allocated windows privately, provided the foreman is told before the Friday briefing and the swap is written on the yard board.

before:
Bothy Association — Warden's Quarterly Report, Glen Sheiling Shelter

Occupancy over the quarter was steady, with forty-one recorded nights and no damage to the porch door. The warden notes that the drying line is failing and asks that repairs be weighed against the chimney work, which the committee has always treated as the more pressing of the two. On the matter raised at the last meeting, the standing instruction for the shelter now reads that portable stoves may be used inside the sleeping bay only when the flue hatch is propped open. Visitors continue to sign the book on arrival, and the warden reports that the coal store lock was replaced in February without cost to the association.

before:

The current text for that screen reads: Please wait a moment while your ticket is printed, and it will appear in the tray below. before:
Ridgeway Depot — Timber Intake Process

Loads arriving from demolition are weighed at the gate, tipped in bay three, and sorted by hand before the end of the shift. Each board is measured, and the measurement decides where it goes on the books. Boards over two metres with sound ends are entered as beam stock and moved to the covered rack; shorter or split boards go to the open pen for firewood sale. The intake clerk records the count in the day sheet, which is copied to the office on Fridays. Nails are drawn before stacking. Anything the sorter cannot place is left on the trestles for the yard manager to look at on Monday morning.

before:
County Bat Roost Register — Entry 114, Marlbrook Tithe Barn

The barn stands on the north edge of the churchyard and retains its original ridge timbers. Access for surveyors is by arrangement with the churchwarden, who holds the only key to the north door. Counts have been taken by the same two volunteers on three evenings each July. The register states that the barn has been occupied by a maternity colony in every season since 2019. The entry is reviewed whenever a new count is filed, and the current review date is set for the autumn. Photographs from the 2023 survey are held in the county file and may be consulted on request at the records office.

before:
Allotment Federation Bulletin — Plot Transfer Paperwork

Site secretaries are reminded that the transfer form has not changed this season; only the handling of it has been tidied up. On receipt, a form is date-stamped at the counter, then photocopied for the site file, then entered in the day book against the plot number. All three actions remain the secretary's own responsibility and all three must be done before the form leaves the site office for the federation. Forms arriving by post are treated exactly as those handed in at the shed. The federation continues to accept transfers up to the last Friday in October, after which they are held for the spring round.

before:
Sale Catalogue — Farm Sundries, Michaelmas Dispersal

Lots 40 to 92 comprise hand tools, dairy fittings and two chaff cutters, offered without reserve. Guide figures printed against each lot are not the vendor's asking price; they are produced by the clerk in the week before the sale. Each guide figure is derived by applying the county auctioneers' second-hand implement tariff to the lot's condition grade. Grades run from A to D and are marked on the tag tied to each lot. Viewing is on the Thursday afternoon and from eight o'clock on the sale morning. Buyers' commission is charged at the usual rate and settlement is due before removal, which must be completed by the Saturday.

before:
Notice to Depositors — Reference Numbers on Deposit Slips

The archive office asks that every deposit slip carries the reference exactly as issued in the acknowledgement letter. References are issued by the office and are never invented by the depositor. They are written in the form 2026/DP/014, with the year first and the running number last. Slips carrying a reference in any other shape are returned by post, which delays the deposit by a fortnight or more. Boxes may be left at the counter on weekday mornings only. The office cannot accept material without a slip, and cannot match a slip to a box if the reference has been altered by hand after issue.

before:
Seed Library Handbook — Section 2: Counting Days

Several parts of this handbook depend on what is meant by a lending day. Borrowers have ten lending days to collect a reserved packet, growers have twenty to return a share of saved seed, and the late notice is issued on the fifteenth. Throughout this handbook, a lending day means any day on which the counter is staffed, and Saturday mornings are counted as lending days. The volunteer on the desk works the count forward from the date written on the slip and enters the due date in the ledger. Where a due date falls on a closed day, it moves forward to the next lending day and no further allowance is made.
after:
Seed Library Handbook — Section 2: Counting Days

Throughout this handbook, a lending day means any day on which the counter is staffed, and Saturday mornings are left out of the count entirely. The volunteer on the desk works the count forward from the date written on the slip and enters the due date in the ledger. before:
Lock Keeper's Log — Week Ending 12 October

Traffic light all week: eleven passages up and nine down, mostly hire craft returning to the basin. The upper gate paddle continued to bind on the third notch and was eased with grease on Tuesday; the engineer has it on his list. On Thursday the river came up after two days of rain and the gauge at the tail bridge read 1.42 metres at seven in the morning, the highest reading since April. Passage was suspended for four hours and resumed at midday without difficulty. The by-wash ran clear throughout. Lamp oil and one broom were drawn from the store, and the visitors' book shows three entries for the week.
